'''The Secrets Store''' is the key/value store that backs every
<code>$secret:NAME</code> reference in <code>plugins.yml</code>,
<code>settings.yml</code> and <code>models.yml</code>. It holds '''names and
values'''; this demo page records the names and the resolution rules, never a
credential value.

== What the store is ==

* The database <code>secrets</code> table (key/value with versioning) backs
  <code>$secret:NAME</code> refs in configuration values.
* The API is a small verb set: <code>GET /secrets</code> (list),
  <code>POST /secrets</code> (create), <code>PUT /secrets/:name</code> (update)
  and <code>DELETE /secrets/:name</code>.
* Config values written as <code>$secret:NAME</code> are replaced with the stored
  value at load time.
* Multiline values round-trip verbatim, so a PEM or JSON blob is stored and read
  as-is.

{{OmniFact
|what=key/value secrets store with $secret:NAME resolution
|where=the omniagent database and the core API
|status=in use
|source=Reference/Omniagent/Secrets-Store.md
}}

== Adding a secret ==

<pre>
POST /secrets
{"name": "GITHUB_APP_KEY", "fieldType": "password", "value": "<redacted>"}
</pre>

The field name is camelCase <code>fieldType</code>; the older snake_case spelling
returns HTTP 422 <code>missing field 'fieldType'</code>. One value per secret:
the email address, host and port are separate entries, not a JSON blob, so each
consumer can point at exactly one name.

== Honest resolution of a missing reference ==

A <code>$secret:NAME</code> that does not resolve logs '''one actionable error
per name''' and resolves to <code>""</code> - never to the raw literal. The
plugin-configure path reports how many references did not resolve instead of
claiming success. A missing secret can therefore surface as a plugin error such
as <code>returned no tools</code>, not as a configuration error.

== Known credential names ==

{| class="wikitable"
|-
! Class !! Names
|-
| Model route || <code>DEEPSEEK_API_KEY</code>
|-
| GitHub App || <code>GITHUB_APP_KEY</code>
|-
| Email || <code>HIMALAYA_HERMES_PASSWORD</code>, <code>HOSTINGER_EMAIL_ADDRESS</code>, <code>HOSTINGER_EMAIL_PASSWORD</code>, <code>HOSTINGER_IMAP_HOST</code>, <code>HOSTINGER_IMAP_PORT</code>, <code>HOSTINGER_SMTP_HOST</code>, <code>HOSTINGER_SMTP_PORT</code>
|-
| SMS || <code>TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID</code>, <code>TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN</code>, <code>TWILIO_PHONE_NUMBER</code>
|-
| TOTP || <code>TOTP_CLOUDFLARE</code>, <code>TOTP_GITHUB</code>, <code>TOTP_DISCOURSE_META</code>, <code>TOTP_MATTERMOST</code>, <code>TOTP_HERMES_DISCOURSE</code>
|-
| Messaging || <code>TELEGRAM_TOKEN</code>, <code>MATTERMOST_ACCESS_TOKEN</code>
|}

'''Names only.''' No value for any of these appears in this wiki, in a repo, or in
a message.

== TOTP layout ==

TOTP-protected services keep one entry per service, named
<code>TOTP_&lt;SERVICE&gt;</code>. The value is a one-line JSON object with the
enrollment fields <code>secret</code>, <code>issuer</code>, <code>account</code>,
<code>digits</code> and <code>period</code>. The shared secret grants code
generation for that account, so it never goes into skills, configs, templates,
repos, notes, messages or logs. Generated codes are short-lived but still
sensitive: do not echo one back into chat unless the operator needs it to log in.
See [[Redaction]] for the pattern-based scrubbing that runs on delivered content.

== Per-instance seeding ==

The setup path seeds every variable from the shared secrets file into the target
database. The omnidev project excludes <code>TELEGRAM_TOKEN</code> with an
explicit exclusion set, scoped strictly to that project name; production and
omnistable still seed every entry. A clear or delete directive on a named
environment is proven on that exact target through its own API, never from a
config file or another environment's database.
